Esri, CGIAR, USGS | Texas Parks & Wildlife, Esri, TomTom, Garmin, SafeGraph, FAO, METI/NASA, USGS, Bureau of Land Management, EPA, NPS, USFWS | Mid-Region Council of Governments, 505-247-1750, www.mrcog-nm.gov
Powered by Esri

AMPA

The Albuquerque Metropolitan Planning Area (AMPA) is MRMPO's planning area.

This area was revised in 2012-2013, with approval for revising by the Metropolitan Planning Board (MTB) on September 21, 2012, and the Governor of New Mexico on February 27, 2013.

The area was maintained in 2023, with approval for maintaining by the MTB on August 18, 2023, and by the New Mexico Department of Transportation (NMDOT) on February 1, 2024.

MRCOG & MRRTPO

The Mid-Region Council of Governments (MRCOG) region includes the AMPA (described above) and the Mid-Region Regional Transportation Planning Organization (MRRTPO). Local Planning Assistance (LPA) is offered throughout the MRCOG region by the Regional Planning Program (RPP).

Tribal Areas

This map uses Land Area Representations (LAR) from the Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA) to represent tribal areas. The To'Hajiilee Navajo Nation Chapter is also represented by BIA data. The Ojo Encino Navajo Nation Chapter and the 19 Pueblos District were manually digitized. 

Roadway Functional Classification

The Functional Classification system was updated in 2025. The system was approved by the MTB on October 17, 2025, and by the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) on April 1, 2026.

Only select Local roads are shown. Any road not shown should be considered a Local road.

Adjusted Urban Areas

The Albuquerque and Los Lunas Adjusted Urban Areas include all roadways classified as "urban." Roadways outside of these areas are "rural." These areas were approved by the MTB on August 18, 2023, and by NMDOT on February 1, 2024.

Road Owners

Road ownership is modeled and should not be considered authoritative. It is based on data from state and local agencies. Please contact us to correct any mistakes (gis@mrcog-nm.gov).

Other Areas

NMDOT District Boundaries are provided by NMDOT. 

County boundaries are provided by the US Census Bureau.

Incorporated Places (i.e., municipalities) are provided by the municipalities themselves and/or the New Mexico Taxation & Revenue Department (NMTRD).
